identifiedBug.description: Bootstrap/restore created a receiver-preserving facade containing only the older scalar getters. It omitted both private word-version markers and all word methods, so nested startup/restore could silently use legacy integer transport while live raw projections used words.
identifiedBug.runtimeObservation: Same-view trace: nestedLists=true, integerApplied=false, invoked function not in word-wrapper WeakSet, integer result zero before and after thenable guard. Last word-call record belonged to another projection/read.
identifiedBug.deterministicReproduction: Valid complete word API plus legacy getter traps failed both document startup and checkpoint restore before forwarding; both passed after forwarding.
identifiedBug.testSetupCorrection: First attempt tried assigning configurable but readonly fake heading/start methods and failed in setup. Replaced via defineProperty, then obtained the actual expected-false bootstrap reproduction.

fix: Capture and validate the complete nested-only word capability once, preserve markers and receiver-bound raw word methods in the facade. Unknown, partial and async capabilities fail with exactly-once raw projection cleanup. Scalar-only and genuine legacy modules remain compatible. Base/flat bootstraps do not probe these private capabilities.
adjacentFixedBug: Facade invocation converted asynchronous legacy method results into undefined, permitting absence probes to accept forbidden async returns. Deterministic rejected-Promise test previously returned successful bootstrap. Raw results now reach the strict consumer's thenable containment and validation; test rejects without double cleanup.

regressions.signedFacadeRecordTest: Same record identity, raw receiver, indices and exact safe signed boundaries; method snapshot resists later replacement, helper never owns raw cleanup

forwardingOnlyPair.scope: Predates raw async-return preservation; retained independently.

limits: Fixes concrete facade omissions and async acceptance. Repeated packed stress, exact replay, native input and accepted size/latency gates remain open; no claim all historical WebKit faults are resolved.
